reasoning_summary: The run is mechanically sound. It completed, the Courant number is 0.73198, the inlet is uniform, the blockage ratio is 0.0125 and the force reference matches the problem. The record shows 10 stationary cycles, after a transient that ended at 67.226 convective units. The mean-drag CI95 is 0.0034414 and the half-window difference is 0.0048991. The drift of 0.010692 is still about a third of the 3 % tolerance.

The convection scheme is Gauss upwind, which is first-order. The cell size is coarse: representative size 0.45745 D, 30580 cells in total, and the last wake cell is 1.0209 D. First-order upwind adds numerical diffusion that is not small relative to the physical viscosity at this Reynolds number (100.0). The effective Reynolds number is therefore lower than the configured one. That would bias both the mean drag and the shedding frequency.

The evidence has no mesh-refinement or scheme-sensitivity study. There is only one run, R0. The small statistical scatter measures the sampling error in time. It says nothing about the spatial and scheme discretization error, which is the dominant risk against a 3 % target on two quantities.

The Strouhal estimates agree with each other (0.12614, 0.12581, FFT 0.12605). The reported-setup frequency resolution is 0.013333, about 10 % of St. That is far coarser than the 3 % tolerance, so it cannot confirm 3 % accuracy for the reported value. The FFT agreement only shows internal consistency. It does not show that the shedding frequency of the upwind-damped solution matches the true one.

Because of the first-order scheme, the coarse wake and the missing verification, I cannot trust mean_drag_coefficient (1.2674) or strouhal_number (0.12581) to within 3 %. Medium confidence, since the discretization error is not quantified in the evidence.
